name: LT1360 / LT1361 / LT1362 (50MHz, 800V/us C-Load bipolar single/dual/quad)
tagline: Linear Tech's 50MHz/800V/us C-Load bipolar op amp. Sound-card op-amp swappers rate it for DAC I/V stages and describe it as 'extremely clear and airy'.
technology: A voltage-feedback op amp built on Linear Technology's complementary bipolar process. It is unity-gain stable and belongs to LTC's C-Load high-speed family (LT1354 to LT1365). The C-Load design keeps it stable with any capacitive load: it senses the pole the load puts on the output and adds compensation at the gain node. The input stage is matched and high-impedance and the part slews like a current-feedback amplifier; that part of the description comes from the family text in the LT1364/LT1365 datasheet.

lineage.notes: A 'Linear Technology Corporation 1994' copyright appears in the family datasheet text returned by search (LT1361/LT1362 or LT1364/LT1365 datasheet; medium confidence as an introduction date). In the C-Load family, the LT1357 (25MHz, 600V/us) and LT1363 (70MHz, 1000V/us) have separate datasheets, and the LT1364/LT1365 datasheet names the LT1361/LT1362 as the 'Lower Power Version of LT1364/LT1365, VOS = 1mV, 4mA/Amplifier'. No second source.

Datasheets are served from analog.com (1360fa.pdf, 13612fa.pdf). ADI has issued two marking-only PCNs covering the LT1361CS8 (21_0060: ink to laser top mark on 8-SOIC; 24_0236: bottom trace code moved to top laser mark). No die or wafer-fab change PCN was found.

reputation.summary: A niche favourite of sound-card op-amp swappers (mostly Asus Xonar Essence ST/STX), used mainly in the I/V stage after current-output DACs. One user paired it with an LME49720 and described the result as an 'extremely clear and airy sound'. Some Xonar/Head-Fi threads list it with the LT1028, OPA627, OPA827, LT1364 and LT1469 as I/V or DAC-output choices. Users also call it forgiving of poor bypassing. All of this is subjective forum opinion from a handful of posts; no bench measurements (Audio Science Review, Samuel Groner or similar) were found.
typical_uses: I/V conversion after current-output DACs (Asus Xonar Essence ST/STX)
wideband amplifiers, buffers, active filters, cable drivers (vendor applications)
caveats: Forum posts say the dual comes only in SOIC-8, so DIP-8 sockets need an adapter. A DIP-8 LT1361CN8#PBF appears only in a part sitemap and is unconfirmed.
Bipolar inputs with fairly high bias current (LCSC parametric: 300 nA) and up to 1 mV offset: expect DC offset with high source or feedback impedances.
A 50MHz, 800V/us part: needs a tight layout and short decoupling. Socket adapters add parasitics, although the C-Load design is stable with capacitive loads.
Up to 5 mA per amplifier. The 34 mA output-current figure (distributor data) suggests it should not drive low-impedance headphones directly.
Descriptors come from a small number of subjective posts; no measurements were found.

silicon_changes.when: PCN 21_0060, 11 Nov 2021 (Rev -, Rev A and Rev B exist)
silicon_changes.identification: Older parts have an ink top mark and newer parts have a laser top mark. This applies to 8-SOICN packages assembled at ADPG, UTAC and Carsem.
silicon_changes.summary: Marking only, not a die change. On legacy Linear 8-SOICN products the top mark changed from ink to laser. This entry records both marking styles as genuine. The completeness-sweep mention of 21_0060 is merged here.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - marking change only; same die and package.
silicon_changes.verification: WebSearch confirms that PCN 21_0060 Rev B (11 Nov 2021) is an ADI notice covering Linear 8-SOIC parts (LT1363CS8, LT1364CS8). The LT1361CS8 listing and the ink-to-laser detail come from an earlier pass. The PDF itself was not read.

silicon_changes.when: PCN 22_0241 (Rev - and Rev A; Rev A dated 18 Dec 2023 per search summary). Effective from date code 2242.
silicon_changes.identification: By date code: parts coded 2242 or later use the new epoxy. There is no visible marking difference.
silicon_changes.summary: Assembly material change. The epoxy formulation changed from Henkel 8290 to Henkel 8290A (Ablestik 8290 is a die-attach paste). ADI states no impact to fit, form or function, with improved reliability. The die and wafer process are unchanged.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low - assembly material change; same die.
silicon_changes.verification: A WebSearch summary of PCN 22_0241 lists LT1361, LT1362 and LT1364 among the affected LT13xx/LT14xx op amps. It gives the change as Henkel 8290 to 8290A epoxy, effective from date code 2242, with no fit, form or function impact. The PDF itself was not read.

silicon_changes.when: October 2024 (PCN 24_0236 Rev -, 8 Oct 2024; companion PCN 24_0234 Rev -)
silicon_changes.identification: Older parts carry the trace code on the bottom of the package. Newer parts carry it in the top-side laser mark. The change is identified by date code.
silicon_changes.summary: Marking only, not a die change. The bottom-side trace-code mark moved into the top-side laser mark to standardise marking across ADI packages. ADI states no impact to form, fit, function or reliability. The completeness-sweep mentions of 24_0234 and 24_0236 are merged here.
silicon_changes.verification: WebSearch confirms that PCN 24_0234 and 24_0236 are the bottom-to-top trace-code marking migration, with no form, fit, function or reliability impact. The LT1361CS8#PBF listing comes from an earlier pass. The per-part list was not read.

counterfeit_notes: No counterfeit or remarking reports specific to the LT1360/LT1361/LT1362 were found. Genuine LT1361CS8 parts come in several marking styles: an ink top mark on older parts, a laser top mark after ADI PCN 21_0060, and, after PCN 24_0236 (Oct 2024), the trace code on top instead of the bottom. A marking-style difference alone does not prove a fake. Buy from ADI or authorized distributors; pulled or grey-market high-speed LTC parts are common on marketplace sites. A DIP-8 'LT1361' deserves scrutiny: the DIP-8 orderable LT1361CN8#PBF appears only in a part sitemap and is unconfirmed.

The cds.linear.com datasheet URLs and linear.com/product/LT1360 are inferred URL patterns (archive seeds only).

The ADI lifecycle label (Production/NRND) for the LT1361 and LT1362 was not explicitly seen; the LT1360 shows Production.

revision_chain_notes: LINEAR TECHNOLOGY / ADI 13612f (LT1361/LT1362): the chain runs from the original 13612f (not found; c.1994 per the copyright line) to 13612fa, the current copy at analog.com (date not shown). The missing link is any copy clearly identified as the original 13612f, and the printed date of the 'fa' re-issue. The copies to check first for pre-A content are the Carnegie Observatories lab PDF (instrumentation.obs.carnegiescience.edu/ccd/parts/LT1361.pdf) and the old low-numbered alldatasheet entries 70422 (LT1361) and 70423 (LT1362). No search summary showed a revision for them. LINEAR TECHNOLOGY / ADI 1360f (LT1360): the chain runs from the original 1360f (copyright 1994 confirmed in the search summary; the copy itself was not found) to 1360fa, the current analog.com copy, which the ADI web listing dates 08/28/2007. The missing link is a copy that holds the original 1360f; the Scribd upload 695059610 and alldatasheet 70421 are candidates, revision not shown. The family had no second sources and no TI, National or other vendor editions. Five archive seed URLs are unverified guesses I built from Linear's usual file-name patterns (www.linear.com/pdf/<code>.pdf and cds.linear.com/docs/en/datasheet/<code>.pdf) plus the /product/LT1360 page. No search result showed them; they are only candidates for a Wayback lookup. The linear.com/pdf/13612f.pdf and 1360f.pdf forms of the original edition would be the key Wayback lookups. None of the 4 search summaries showed any footer print code (LT/TP or LT/GP), so no revision letter could be pinned to any mirror.
